NOTE B: STRATEGIC INVESTMENT IN SUBSIDIARY Overview On April 17, 2026, with respect to our wholly owned subsidiary, Aerojet Rocketdyne Holdings, Inc. (“AR”), which operates as our Missile Solutions segment, we entered into a definitive agreement (the “DoW Investment Agreement”) with the United States Department of War (“DoW” or the “Investor”). The DoW Investment Agreement provided for the issuance and sale of 10,000 shares of Redeemable AR Series A Convertible Preferred Stock (the “Subsidiary Series A Preferred Stock”) par value of $ 0.0001 per share and stated value of $ 100,000 per share, and pre-initial public offering (“IPO”) and, upon a Qualified IPO (as defined in the DoW Investment Agreement), post-IPO warrants (collectively the “Subsidiary Warrants”), for an aggregate purchase price of $ 1 billion, which is the initial face value of the Subsidiary Series A Preferred Stock. The Subsidiary Series A Preferred Stock payout options include one of the following: (i) a liquidation preference equal to face value of the preferred shares plus 7 % cumulative annual dividends, compounded quarterly (the “Liquidation Preference”); (ii) an automatic conversion into common stock of our wholly owned subsidiary AXYV Inc. (“AXYV”), at a 20 % discount to the IPO stock price upon a Qualified IPO on or before December 31, 2027; or (iii) either Investor conversion on demand or redemption on or after April 17, 2031, at fair value, if a Qualified IPO does not occur by December 31, 2027. Under the DoW Investment Agreement, we are expected to use commercially reasonable efforts to consummate a Qualified IPO. The options are mutually exclusive and are dependent on achieving specified milestones. The purpose of the investment is to strengthen the U.S. defense industrial base by providing funding for the Missile Solutions segment to expand and modernize its facilities, accelerate research and development, and increase production capacity for critical technologies. The fair value of the investment exceeds the proceeds as it simultaneously provides financing, the opportunity to substantially expand an existing commercial relationship, and the benefit of an anchor investor whose participation tangibly demonstrates the Missile Solutions segment’s strong long-term business prospects. The DoW Investment Agreement contains customary representations, warranties, and covenants by us and the Investor. Under the terms of the DoW Investment Agreement, AR may redeem, or the Investor may require the redemption of, the Subsidiary Series A Preferred Stock and Subsidiary Warrants held by the Investor under certain conditions. Use of Proceeds Under terms of the DoW Investment Agreement, net proceeds of $ 973 million are to be used to fund development and construction activities for expanding our missile manufacturing capacity and capabilities within our Missile Solutions segment. We intend to use the remaining net proceeds, if any, for general corporate purposes. The net proceeds are included in the “Proceeds from issuance of subsidiary Series A preferred stock, net” line item in our Condensed Consolidated Statement of Cash Flows as Net cash used in financing activities. Conversion Upon Qualified IPO On or Before December 31, 2027. Upon completion of a Qualified IPO, the Subsidiary Series A Preferred Stock will convert into common stock of AXYV (“AXYV Common Stock”) at a 20 % discount to the public offering price in the Qualified IPO. The conversion terms are designed to provide the holder with a fixed return settled in a variable number of shares of AXYV Common Stock. The Investor’s ownership percentage would be determined based on the valuation of AXYV at the time of a Qualified IPO. Fair Value Conversion or Redemption After December 31, 2027. If a Qualified IPO does not occur on or before December 31, 2027, the redemption price calculation methodology varies depending on whether specified milestones have been achieved by such date. If such milestones are not achieved by December 31, 2027, the redemption price would be calculated by applying a contractual premium of 110 % to the Liquidation Preference. If the milestones are achieved by December 31, 2027, the Investor can convert the Subsidiary Series A Preferred Stock at any time (including in the case of an IPO after December 31, 2027), or a redemption on or after April 17, 2031 could occur. The Investor’s conversion rate will be determined based on the face value of the Subsidiary Series A Preferred Stock ($ 1 billion) divided by 15 times 2026 AXYV earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization (“EBITDA”). The redemption price would be calculated on or after April 17, 2031, and would equal the greater of (i) the Liquidation Preference or (ii) the fair market value, calculated in the same manner as noted above. Redemption Upon Sale of AXYV. If there is a sale of AXYV before a Qualified IPO, or after December 31, 2027 but prior to a Qualified IPO and specified milestones have not been achieved, the redemption price would be calculated by applying a contractual premium of 110 % to the Liquidation Preference. If specified milestones have been achieved, the Investor is entitled to receive cash equal to the greater of the Liquidation Preference or a pro forma ownership percentage which is calculated as the face value of the Subsidiary Series A Preferred Stock divided by 15 times 2026 AXYV EBITDA. Conversion and Redemption Feature Embedded Derivatives . Certain of the conversion and redemption features represent embedded derivatives. These features of the Subsidiary Series A Preferred Stock were bifurcated from the host instrument and recorded as a derivative liability, which is included in the “Subsidiary Series A preferred stock conversion feature” line item in the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheet at its fair value. The derivative liability is measured at fair value each reporting period, with changes recognized in earnings as a component of the “Other non-operating (expense) income, net” line item in our Condensed Consolidated Statement of Operations. Warrants The Subsidiary Warrants entitle the Investor to purchase shares representing 3 % of the AXYV Common Stock, on a fully diluted basis, and consist of pre-IPO warrants exercisable at 100 %, 110 %, and 120 % of the non-IPO common stock price, and post-IPO warrants exercisable at 100 %, 110 %, and 120 % of the Qualified IPO price, which take effect upon a Qualified IPO. The pre-IPO warrants become exercisable only upon (i) the occurrence of certain events outlined in the DoW Investment Agreement and (ii) the passage of time (i.e., on or after December 31, 2027), but only if certain operational conditions are met that are outside the control of the Company and the Investor. The pre-IPO warrants are accounted for as derivative liabilities, included in the “Subsidiary warrants” line item in the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheet, initially measured at fair value with subsequent changes recognized in earnings as a component of the “Other non-operating (expense) income, net” line item in our Condensed Consolidated Statement of Operations. Immediately prior to the Qualified IPO, the pre-IPO warrants will automatically convert into post-IPO warrants of AXYV. Our multi-year capacity expansion in our Missile Solutions segment involves substantial capital commitments and is reliant on our multi-year procurement contracts. In response to the Munitions Acceleration Council (“MAC”) framework initiatives and increased demand, we are executing a multi-year capacity expansion and modernization plan involving more than $3 billion of capital investments through 2030 across our Missile Solutions segment to materially increase annual production capacity for solid rocket motors, divert and attitude control systems, and precision fuzes across priority MAC programs. These large-scale facility build-outs and advanced manufacturing expansions are subject to complex execution and commissioning risks, including: delays in permitting, site preparation, engineering, and construction; extended lead times, delivery delays, or integration challenges for specialized tooling, large-scale propellant mixers, robotics, and automated production systems; technical difficulties in scaling manufacturing processes; and delays in completing rigorous customer and government validation, testing, and qualification milestones required before expanded facilities can achieve full-rate production authorization. The expansions also increase our existing risk of supply chain disruption because of increased production volumes. While we have agreed to multi-year contracts for minimum production volumes for priority MAC missile programs, these contracts require sustained government appropriations across the multi-year performance periods. Although cancellation fees under these multi-year contracts are designed to cover facilitization charges and are higher than our standard terms, cancellation fees may not cover all of our incurred capital expenditures, site preparation costs, long-lead supply commitments, and ongoing facility operating expenses. Furthermore, if orders are canceled, we may be unable to fully utilize this specialized manufacturing footprint or redirect these custom facilities to alternative programs, resulting in unabsorbed overhead, facility underutilization, and unrecovered capital investments. Additionally, achieving target production rates requires rapidly scaling our specialized workforce at these expansion sites, including engineering, assembly, quality assurance, and Environmental, Health and Safety personnel with active security clearances. Bottlenecks in recruitment, training, or government security clearance processing, as well as operational constraints associated with increased energetic mixing volumes and hazardous waste disposal limits, could impede facility ramp milestones. Our long-term funding and production volumes could also be adversely affected by proposed legislative initiatives, including second-source mandates for certain of our missile products and subsystems for which we are the sole supplier. If enacted into law or implemented into DoW procurement strategy, mandatory second sourcing could redirect government funding or future contract awards to competitors or new entrants, reduce our share of program quantities, and undermine the economic assumptions underlying our capital investments, leaving our expanded production lines with excess capacity. Any failure to successfully execute our facility expansion and modernization plans on schedule and within budget, or any cancellation, reduction in appropriations, or legislative reallocation of procurement funding to second sources that leaves capital investments unrecovered, could impair our ability to meet customer delivery commitments on priority missile programs, undermine our competitive position, and adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations, cash flows and equity. _____________________________________________________________________ 40 We depend on our subcontractors and suppliers, and failures in or disruptions to our supply chain could cause our products and or services to be produced or delivered in an untimely or unsatisfactory manner.
